findings.title: Serialize index creation per resource key
findings.body: Locking only the cache assignment allows concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource. For example, a search and a write-event handler can both miss the cache and build separate in-memory indexes. If the event handler publishes its index and applies the event before the other build finishes, the other build can overwrite the cache with an older snapshot, losing the indexed update. GetIndex previously blocked behind the build lock, preventing this interleaving. Keep builds for different keys parallel, but coordinate creation and publication for the same key.

findings.title: Synchronize TotalDocs with cache publication
findings.body: The new startup log calls s.search.TotalDocs() after starting the write-event consumer. That consumer can build an index for a previously uncached resource and publish it concurrently. The Bleve implementation of TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu, so this new call can race with cache writes and terminate the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. Protect the cache iteration with the read lock, or take a protected snapshot before counting documents.

findings.title: Preserve rejection of requests after Stop
findings.body: Removing the Init checks also removes the stopped-service guard: Stop sets s.initErr to a stopping/stopped error, which subsequent RPCs previously returned through Init. Create, Update, and Delete now proceed directly to the backend after Stop. In the SQL backend, Stop only cancels polling and leaves database operations usable, so these requests can successfully persist changes after the server has stopped processing watch/index events. Replace the lazy-initialization checks with an explicit lifecycle-state check rather than dropping this protection.
